packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- My standing context (a memory index loaded at session start, not the packet) mentions a "Stams pilot" in a fragment-identification project, and the images carry pencil shelfmarks "Stams, STA, Frg. 241r" / "241v". No proposed identification of the work or author was revealed to me and I have not tried to identify it. Rubrics quoted below ("De quatuor coronatis", "De sancto theodoro", "De nomine sci martini") are read from the leaf itself.
- I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..018 in this directory (I listed the directory to get file names; I did not open packet.json). Nothing else done beyond the brief.
- [cut] = lost to trimming; [illegible] = present but unreadable to me; expansions in ( ) are proposals; "?" follows uncertain readings. I have not supplied lost text.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001: overview of an opened bifolium, face 241r. Two pages, each one column, ~38-40 ruled lines, brown ink, gothic textualis; a smaller, more compressed hand than packet-01? (not compared further). Leaf is abraded and darkened, especially a vertical dark stain band along the right side of the left page and the gutter; ink is faded across much of the left page.
- Left page (241r-left): red rubric at line end "De quatuor coronatis" (line 1); large red initial Q?/O with long descending red tail (about 9 lines); second red rubric "De sancto theodoro" with large red T (~3 lines); third red rubric "De nomine sci martini" with a red M (~3 lines). Lower margin below the text block has later inscriptions in other hands (a cursive line and a line of large textura/court-hand letters, plus a purple stamp/pen mark); not transcribed. Top-left margin has scraps ("[?]erdi" etc.), unread.
- Right page (241r-right): no rubric titles; red paragraph marks (C-shaped) at several section openings; interlinear additions (e.g. "aplor(um)", "sanguis"), marginal letters with caret marks ("A patris", "A expositi?") on the right margin = insertions. Lower ~quarter of page blank (text ends ~line 30 with an underlined/emphasized close?). A vertical red stroke below the last line.
- image-010: overview of face 241v. Left page: full column, red paragraph marks; right page: full column, red paragraph marks; outer margins carry small insertion notes ("spiritualia", "scire possunt", "patri"?). Many lines carry interlinear corrections.
- Interpretation (tentative): continuous prose; 241r-left is narrative divided by rubricated chapter titles; 241r-right and 241v read as an expository/discursive treatment (numbered "Tercio / Quarto" divisions, authorities cited by abbreviated name: "aug(ustinus)", "amb(rosius)", "ieronimus"?). No separate gloss apparatus visible.
- Tiles: 002-005 down 241r-left; 006-009 down 241r-right; 011-014 down 241v-left; 015-018 down 241v-right. Overlapping lines between successive tiles are marked "overlap".

SELECTED AREAS: I read the rubric openings and as much connected prose as I could on all four pages. 241r-left is very faded and stained on its right third; many line ends there are [illegible]. 241r-right is the weakest page (abraded, faded): I give the better lines only. 241v is clearer and is read nearly completely. A multispectral/UV image of 241r would help considerably.
